title: Produce byte-identical PDF output and hashes
description: Canonically order and encode renderer inputs and suppress nondeterministic PDF metadata so identical normalized inputs produce byte-identical PDF bytes and the same content hash.
acceptanceCriteria: Canonical input ordering covers pages, positions, scene nodes, text runs, resources, diagnostics metadata, and optional translation
Equivalent object insertion order and source-unit formatting do not change PDF bytes
Creation dates, random IDs, subset names, compression choices, and document metadata are fixed or deterministically derived
Repeated generation from identical normalized inputs produces byte-identical bytes
The content hash is calculated from final PDF bytes with a documented stable algorithm
A normalized input change that affects output changes bytes and hash

steps.details: Specify versioned field ordering, stable node/resource sorting, numeric encoding, Unicode normalization, and excluded presentation/source fields before renderer invocation.
Configure or post-process library-generated timestamps, IDs, subset prefixes, metadata, object ordering, and compression parameters so they are fixed or input-derived.
Compute a versioned SHA-256 or equivalently documented content hash over the exact downloadable byte array and return it with normalized generation metadata.
Generate the same canonical fixture multiple times and in fresh process/browser contexts, then compare every byte and hash.
Reorder source object keys and use equivalent normalized source units to prove identical output, then change printable text or geometry and prove bytes and hash change.

technicalNotes: Hash the final bytes, not only the logical scene or pre-render canonical payload.
Document any selected-library limitation that prevents deterministic control; do not weaken byte-identical acceptance silently.
